calculationRules: Catalog maximum ratings are not VX4800 design loads and cannot be copied into product calculations as applied loads.

Rigid-body polar inertia from the rotating mass map is a screening and drive-input quantity only; suspended elements can lag during acceleration and braking and require T1/T2/T3/T4 physical correlation.
Every numeric input must carry an evidence class and source; assumptions remain visibly labelled and cannot silently become controlled production values.
Drive sizing must include acceleration demand plus bearing resistance, transmission losses, drag, imbalance and other approved resistances rather than inertia alone.
Bearing/support calculations must include drive pretension/tangential reactions, brake reactions and structural mounting stiffness where applicable.
Fault-stop and retention cases must use approved failure scenarios from the released risk assessment rather than arbitrary emergency factors.
A load case may become verified only after its calculation is independently checked and its physical-correlation requirement, where applicable, is satisfied.

loadCases.name: static gravity and combined bearing load
loadCases.purpose: Establish primary static gravity, radial eccentricity and overturning-moment inputs for bearing/support selection and structural reactions.
requiredInputs: controlled full rotating mass map including carrier/drive rotating parts

sourceEvidence.source: Issue #9 production S/M/L mass records plus controlled rotating-component mass records

prohibitedAssumptions: do not infer total mass from visual material choice
do not assume CG is exactly on the rotation axis
do not omit drive pretension from support reactions
verificationMethod: supplier combined-load review for exact bearing variant

loadCases.name: jerk-limited start transient
loadCases.purpose: Determine propulsion and support demand during the released start profile while accounting for suspended-field lag rather than treating the field as rigidly attached.
requiredInputs: controlled mass map and screening polar inertia
measured T1/T2 suspended-element lag and damping

sourceEvidence.source: T1/T2 jerk/start response and drive-load correlation

prohibitedAssumptions: do not use rigid-body inertia as the complete suspended-field transient model
do not invent acceleration or jerk from aesthetic animation timing
do not infer final drive torque from test-rig motor rating

loadCases.name: steady nominal operation
loadCases.purpose: Establish nominal continuous drive load, thermal duty, bearing resistance and field offset at 0.36 rpm.
requiredInputs: selected bearing running torque under actual load/preload

sourceEvidence.source: exact selected bearing and drive/reducer data
T1/T2 and later T4 steady-state measurements

prohibitedAssumptions: do not equate low rpm with negligible friction or thermal duty
do not assume zero aerodynamic offset

loadCases.name: maximum approved speed operation
loadCases.purpose: Establish continuous and dynamic effects at the controlled maximum speed of 0.65 rpm without assuming nominal-speed behaviour scales trivially.
requiredInputs: measured field dynamics at maximum approved speed
prohibitedAssumptions: do not linearly scale all nominal results to maximum speed
do not approve dynamic clearances from static/BVH screening alone
verificationMethod: full-field T4 clearance and thermal verification

loadCases.name: controlled normal stop
loadCases.purpose: Determine normal deceleration, stop travel, field excitation and settling requirements using the healthy drive and released motion profile.
prohibitedAssumptions: do not set stop time only from motor capability
do not release restart before measured field settling is controlled

loadCases.name: power-loss and fault stop
loadCases.purpose: Establish required carrier holding/fault-stop torque, energy and suspended-field response when propulsion is removed and the qualified holding path acts.

sourceEvidence.source: exact direct-carrier brake dynamic-stop and thermal capability

prohibitedAssumptions: do not assume static brake holding rating equals dynamic stopping capability
do not weaken holding solely because abrupt stopping excites the field; evaluate controlled fixed-side ride-through only if justified
do not size from rigid-body inertia alone

loadCases.name: safe overspeed validation case
loadCases.purpose: Define a controlled overspeed test point and associated detection/stop demand only after risk assessment establishes what is safe and necessary to validate.

sourceEvidence.source: released risk assessment and validation plan

prohibitedAssumptions: do not invent an overspeed percentage
do not exceed a physically validated safe test condition
do not claim one feedback channel is sufficient before risk allocation

loadCases.name: snag and abnormal added-drag detection
loadCases.purpose: Correlate added mechanical resistance with command-versus-actual motion and drive-load signatures so jam detection can act before unsafe escalation.
prohibitedAssumptions: do not set jam threshold from arbitrary percentage of motor current
do not continue increasing torque indefinitely when brake fails to release or carrier does not move

loadCases.name: mass imbalance and trim
loadCases.purpose: Quantify static first moments, required trim correction and effect of production/replacement variation without moving cable exits.
requiredInputs: per-element or controlled S/M/L production mass records
prohibitedAssumptions: do not use nominal catalog/material density instead of production mass records
do not move controlled suspension coordinates for balance correction
do not invent trim capacity before variation is known

loadCases.name: transmission-disconnect holding
loadCases.purpose: Prove the required holding/fault path survives loss of the positive drive transmission and does not rely on gearbox or belt/gear continuity.
prohibitedAssumptions: do not credit motor/gearbox brake through the failed transmission as the only carrier holding path
do not call service lock the normal fault brake

loadCases.name: mechanical service-lock proof case
loadCases.purpose: Establish structural proof and mis-engagement requirements for the positive access lock independent of motor/brake torque.

sourceEvidence.source: service-lock proof, partial-engagement and cycle tests

prohibitedAssumptions: do not derive the lock load from motor stall torque alone
do not invent proof factor before structural/risk methodology is approved
do not rely on software index as engagement proof

loadCases.name: primary-support failure and secondary-retention engagement
loadCases.purpose: Establish abnormal catch loads, engagement travel and fixed-frame reactions for explicitly selected primary-support failure modes.
prohibitedAssumptions: do not apply a generic drop factor without an approved physical failure model
do not assume one local capture point represents distributed retention
do not claim coverage of structural failure modes not actually bypassed by the retention attachments
verificationMethod: controlled simulated engagement and post-test inspection

loadCases.name: manual recovery restrained state
loadCases.purpose: Verify forces and access sequence for recovery from a fault when normal drive or brake release procedures are unavailable, without uncontrolled free motion.
requiredInputs: manual release tooling/force data if selected
restoration sequence for normal holding path
prohibitedAssumptions: do not permit uncontrolled freewheel
do not release the brake/drive before positive restraint
do not improvise force on the carrier when the service index cannot be reached
